scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person in question is a 26-year-old man who took his dad's business idea. His dad is 55, introverted, intelligent but not good at executing ideas. The son describes himself as more impulsive and hot-headed but good at getting things done. He took the idea, got IP rights, started the business two years ago, and it's been a success, making six figures and with potential for millions in the next five years.

When he told his dad, the dad was upset, called him an asshole, felt betrayed, and nearly cried. The son's mom and granddad support him, but the sister supports the dad. The son offered 20% of profits, which was rejected.

So, the question is: Is the son's action morally acceptable?

First, I need to consider the moral aspects here. Stealing an idea is a form of theft, but in this case, it's a family situation. The son took the idea without permission, which could be seen as stealing. However, he argues that his dad couldn't execute it, so he took action to make it successful.

On one hand, the dad came up with the idea, so it's his intellectual property. The son used it without permission, which is wrong. On the other hand, the dad wasn't able to do anything with it, so the son took initiative and made it successful, which could be seen as a positive outcome.

I also need to consider the emotional impact. The dad felt betrayed, which is a strong emotion. The son's actions caused significant distress in the family, leading to arguments and a breakdown in relationships.

Another point is the offer of 20% profits. The son tried to make amends by sharing the success, but the dad refused. This shows that the dad is not just upset about the money but about the principle of the idea being taken.

I think morally, taking someone else's idea without permission is wrong, even if the outcome is positive. It's about respecting ownership and consent. The son could have approached the dad to collaborate or get permission instead of taking it without discussion.

Additionally, the emotional harm caused to the dad and the family dynamics are significant. Actions that cause such distress, even with good intentions, can be morally questionable.

So, considering all these factors, I would lean towards the action being morally unacceptable.
